mainTopic: What counts as forbidden benefit under a נדר: feeding animals, marrying a daughter, small favors, and visiting or healing the מודר
overview: This amud opens at the end of a משנה about feeding the animals of someone who may not benefit from you. רבי אליעזר says a non-kosher animal is fully 'Heaven's', and the חכמים answer that its owner can sell it or feed it to dogs, so it is his. The גמרא then brings רב הונא's ruling that a person may marry his daughter to someone under a נדר of benefit. רבי זירא tests both directions of the vow. He concludes that the case is where the father's property is forbidden to the groom, and the daughter is a בוגרת marrying by her own choice. A ברייתא supports this. Next come small favors that stay allowed despite a vow: filling water, lighting a lamp, roasting a small fish, and giving a 'cup of peace'. The בבל and ארץ ישראל explanations of that cup differ. A ברייתא of יהושע איש עוזא allows feeding the מודר's slaves but not his animals, because slaves are kept for work and animals for fattening. The amud ends with a new משנה about visiting and healing the מודר, which the גמרא explains on the next amud.

steps.title: A non-kosher animal belongs fully to Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The end of the תנא's reasoning in the משנה: a non-kosher animal's life and body both belong to Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A non-kosher animal:] its life and its body belong to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה at the very end of a sentence. The תנא is explaining why feeding someone's non-kosher animal does not count as giving its owner benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner cannot eat a non-kosher animal, so fattening it up does not help him. In the תנא's view, both its life and its body are 'Heaven's,' not the owner's. A kosher animal is different, because the owner can eat its meat.

keyTerms.meaning: To Heaven, meaning not something the owner can use for himself

phrases.english: its life and its body are to Heaven.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a sentence about a non-kosher animal. Its owner can't eat it, so fattening it doesn't help him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי אליעזר's view, feeding a non-kosher animal of the מודר is allowed, because the owner gets no personal benefit from its body. The חכמים reject this in Step 2.

steps.title: The Sages answer that the owner benefits from a non-kosher animal too
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the distinction: the owner can sell a non-kosher animal to non-Jews or feed it to his dogs, so its body is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A non-kosher animal also has its life belonging to Heaven but its body belonging to the owner, because if he wants, he can sell it to non-Jews or feed it to dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on the תנא's reason. They show that a non-kosher animal is also useful to its owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Benefit is not only about eating. The owner can sell the animal or use it as dog food, so its body is his property like a kosher animal's. That means feeding it does give the owner benefit, and there is no difference between kosher and non-kosher animals.
steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים, any way the owner can profit from the animal, even selling it, makes it his. So feeding his animal counts as benefiting him.

phrases.english: They said to him: Even the non-kosher one,
its life is to Heaven and its body is his,
for if he wishes, he can
sell it to non-Jews
or feed it to dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning given in Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The distinction between kosher and non-kosher animals.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes benefit means only eating. Selling or using the animal is also benefit.

steps.title: רב הונא: he may marry his daughter to the one under the vow
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that when one person is forbidden by נדר to get benefit from another, the other may still marry his daughter to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יצחק בר חנניה said in the name of רב הונא: If someone is forbidden by a vow to get benefit from his friend, the friend may marry his daughter to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new ruling from רב הונא. Even with a נדר of benefit between them, a marriage between one man and the other's daughter is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the מודר may not get any benefit from the other person's property. Giving someone your daughter as a wife looks like a big benefit, yet רב הונא allows it. The rest of the גמרא tries to work out exactly which case he means.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that follows the משנה
The person forbidden by vow from getting benefit

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yitzchak bar Chananya said
that Rav Huna said:
One who is forbidden by vow from benefit from his friend,
[the friend] is permitted to marry his daughter to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר חֲנַנְיָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion with a new אמורא ruling about the laws of benefit in this פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying one's daughter to a person under a נדר of benefit is permitted.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks which case רב הונא means
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks what situation רב הונא's ruling describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא discussed it: What case are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא starts to examine רב הונא's ruling. He asks which case it is, which sets up the two options the גמרא is about to test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדר of benefit can go in either direction. Either the father's things are forbidden to the groom, or the groom's things are forbidden to the father. רבי זירא is about to check each direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Discussed it, raised a difficulty about it
With what case are we dealing?

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira discussed it:
With what case are we dealing?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case behind the ruling in Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which direction of the נדר רב הונא's ruling is talking about.

steps.title: If the father's property is forbidden, he is giving the groom a servant
steps.stepSummary: First option rejected: if the father's things are forbidden to the groom, giving him a wife is like giving him a maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is where the bride's father's property is forbidden to the groom, that can't be, because he is handing him a maidservant to serve him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tests the first option and knocks it down. If the groom may not benefit from the father, then marrying him the daughter should be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife takes care of many of her husband's needs. When the father gives his daughter in marriage, it is like giving the groom a servant, and that is a clear benefit from the father. So רב הונא could not be permitting this case.

phrases.english: If we say where the property of the bride's father
is forbidden to the groom,
he is handing him a maidservant to serve him!
phrases.notes: He means the daughter herself. As a wife she will take care of him, so it is like a gift from her father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בְּשֶׁנִּכְסֵי אֲבִי כַלָּה אֲסוּרִין עַל הֶחָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible case raised by the question in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רב הונא is talking about the father's property being forbidden to the groom.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Giving a wife who serves him is a direct benefit from the father, so it should be forbidden.

steps.title: Second option: the groom's property is forbidden to the father
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests the opposite direction: the groom's things are forbidden to the bride's father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where the groom's property is forbidden to the bride's father.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first option failed, רבי זירא tries the other direction. This line sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the groom will support the bride, which might look like a benefit to her father. The suggestion is that רב הונא permits it anyway. רבי זירא is about to show why this reading is also a problem.

phrases.english: Rather, where the groom's property
is forbidden to the bride's father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּנִכְסֵי חָתָן אֲסוּרִין עַל אֲבִי כַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite case after Step 5 rejected the first one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling was about the father's property being forbidden to the groom.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps it is about the groom's property being forbidden to the father.

steps.title: The משנה already taught something bigger, so this is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The second option makes רב הונא's ruling obvious, because the משנה already permits feeding the מודר's wife and children even though he must support them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They already said something greater than this: he may feed [the מודר's] wife and children even though [the מודר] is obligated to support them. And you say it's permitted to marry his daughter to him?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks the second option. If this is the case, רב הונא would be telling us nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the other person to feed the מודר's wife and children, even though the מודר is legally required to feed them. A father has no such duty toward a daughter who marries, so the groom supporting her helps the father even less. A ruling that weak would not need to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: They said something greater than this

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that the marriage should be forbidden. The question is the opposite: in this case it is so obviously allowed that רב הונא would have no reason to say it.

phrases.english: They said something greater than this:
phrases.notes: This points to our own משנה, which allows feeding the מודר's family.

phrases.english: he may feed his wife and his children,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב בִּמְזוֹנוֹתָן,
phrases.english: even though he is obligated in their food,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ מוּתָּר לְהַשִּׂיא לוֹ בִּתּוֹ?!
phrases.english: and you say it is permitted to marry his daughter to him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative case offered in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רב הונא as talking about the groom's property being forbidden to the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already permits a stronger case, so this ruling would add nothing new.

steps.title: The case is a grown daughter marrying by her own consent
steps.stepSummary: Final answer: the father's property is forbidden to the groom, but the daughter is a בוגרת who marries by her own choice, so the benefit is not from her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is where the bride's father's property is forbidden to the groom, and his daughter is a בוגרת, and it is with her consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first option and fixes its problem. The daughter is an adult who decides on her own marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with the first option was that the father seemed to be 'giving' the groom a servant. A בוגרת is not under her father's control and marries by her own choice, so she gives herself, not the father. That makes the ruling a real new teaching and avoids the forbidden benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (going back to an earlier option)
A fully grown young woman, no longer under her father's authority in marriage

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's ruling is about a groom who may not benefit from the bride's father. It is allowed only because the daughter is a בוגרת marrying by her own consent, so the 'gift' comes from her and not from her father.

phrases.english: Actually, where the property of the bride's father
is forbidden to the groom,
and with his daughter grown up, and with her consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּשֶׁנִּכְסֵי אֲבִי כַלָּה אֲסוּרִין עַל הֶחָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first option (Step 5) and adds details that solve its problem, after Step 7 ruled out the second option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case with added details
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father is handing the groom a servant, which is forbidden benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בוגרת marries by her own choice, so the benefit does not come from her father.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא permits the marriage when the father's property is forbidden to the groom, but only if the daughter is a בוגרת marrying with her own consent.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the בוגרת answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing as the last answer: a man may not marry his daughter to the מודר, but he may if she is a בוגרת and agrees herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: if someone is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his friend, the friend may not marry his daughter to him. But he may marry his adult daughter to him if she agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי זירא's final answer said. It is backing up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the same split as the last answer. A regular daughter given by her father would be a gift from the father to the מודר, so it is forbidden. A בוגרת who marries by her own choice is not the father's gift, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the point)
Someone forbidden by a vow to get benefit from another person
A fully grown young woman, no longer under her father's control for marriage

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer to רב הונא's ruling is supported by a ברייתא: a בוגרת who marries by her own choice is not counted as a benefit from her father.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא):
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend:
it is forbidden [for the friend] to marry his daughter to him,
but he may marry him his daughter who is a grown woman, with her consent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the final answer of Step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that רב הונא's ruling is about a בוגרת who marries by her own choice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that forbids marrying a daughter to the מודר but allows it for a בוגרת with her consent.

steps.title: A father who vowed against his son may still do small favors
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב rules that a father who forbade his son to benefit from him, to push him to learn Torah, may still fill a barrel of water and light a lamp for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said: if a man makes a vow forbidding his son to benefit from him, to push him toward Torah study, he may still fill a barrel of water for him and light a lamp for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about small favors that are still allowed even when there is a vow against benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the son may not benefit from his father, רבי יעקב permits these small everyday acts of help. The rule against benefit does not block these simple chores.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes someone else forbidden through a vow
For the sake of Torah study

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said:
One who forbids his son by vow [from benefiting from him] for the sake of Torah study:

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לְמַלּאוֹת לוֹ חָבִית שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: it is permitted to fill a barrel of water for him,
and to light the lamp for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ruling about small acts of help that stay allowed under a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father who vowed against his son may still fill water and light a lamp for him.

steps.title: רבי יצחק adds roasting a small fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the father may also roast a small fish for his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: he may also roast a small fish for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds one more small favor to רבי יעקב's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the same case of the father and son. Roasting a small fish is another small act of help that stays allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
[It is also permitted] to roast a small fish for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another permitted favor to the case in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasting a small fish for the son is also permitted.

steps.title: Giving the מודר a cup of peace is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes רבי יוחנן: a person may give the one forbidden to benefit from him a 'cup of peace' to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend, the friend may still give him a 'cup of peace' to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ruling about a small permitted favor. This one uses the unclear phrase 'cup of peace', which the גמרא will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is any מודר, not just a father and son. רבי יוחנן allows a 'cup of peace', but the ruling does not yet say what that cup is.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'cup of peace', a special cup of drink defined in the next lines

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend:
it is permitted to give him a cup of peace to drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling about permitted small favors, now for any מודר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 'cup of peace' may be given to the מודר.

steps.title: What is a cup of peace?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'cup of peace' is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי יוחנן meant by 'cup of peace'. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is only useful if we know which cup is meant, so the גמרא asks for a definition.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key phrase in Step 12.

steps.title: Two meanings: the mourners' cup or the bathhouse cup
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained it as the cup given in a house of mourning; in ארץ ישראל they said it is the cup drunk at the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they explained it as the cup of the house of mourning. In the West, ארץ ישראל, they said it is the cup of the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different explanations of 'cup of peace', one from the Sages of בבל and one from the Sages of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers describe a common, small drink offered at a set occasion. The two places just disagree about which occasion רבי יוחנן meant.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא תַּרְגִּימוּ: כּוֹס שֶׁל בֵּית הָאֵבֶל.
phrases.english: Here they explained: the cup of the house of mourning.

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִי: כּוֹס שֶׁל בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָץ.
phrases.english: In the West they say: the cup of the bathhouse.
phrases.notes: 'The West' is the usual name in בבל for ארץ ישראל.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בבל: the cup given at a house of mourning. ארץ ישראל: the cup drunk at the bathhouse.

steps.title: Slaves may be fed, but not animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about not feeding the מודר's animal and brings a ברייתא: יהושע איש עוזא allows feeding his Canaanite slaves but not his animals of any kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he may not feed his animal, whether...' It was taught in a ברייתא: יהושע איש עוזא says, he may feed the other person's Canaanite slaves and maidservants, but he may not feed his animal, whether it is non-kosher or kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה about feeding animals. It brings a ברייתא that compares feeding slaves with feeding animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws a line: feeding the מודר's slaves is allowed, but feeding his animals is not, whether kosher or not. Why slaves and animals are treated differently is asked in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יָזוּן אֶת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ בֵּין כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: [The משנה said:] 'And he may not feed his animal, whether etc.'
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on': the משנה continues 'whether non-kosher or kosher.'

phrases.english: It was taught: Yehoshua of Uzza says:
He may feed his Canaanite slaves and maidservants,
but he may not feed his animal,
whether non-kosher or kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a line in the משנה and brings a ברייתא about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may feed the מודר's slaves but not his animals, kosher or non-kosher.

steps.title: Why are slaves different from animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the split between slaves and animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why feeding slaves is allowed but feeding animals is not. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both slaves and animals belong to the מודר, so it seems odd to treat them differently. The גמרא wants the logic.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why feeding slaves is allowed but feeding animals is forbidden.

steps.title: Slaves are for work, animals are for fattening
steps.stepSummary: Slaves are kept to do work, but animals are kept to be fattened, so feeding an animal directly adds to the owner's benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: His Canaanite slaves and maidservants are meant for work. An animal is meant for fattening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: slaves and animals serve different purposes for their owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave is kept to work, so food given to him does not make the owner richer. An animal is kept to be fattened, so feeding it builds up the owner's property and gives him benefit, which the vow forbids.
steps.whatToRemember: Feeding the מודר's slaves is allowed because they are kept for work. Feeding his animals is forbidden because they are kept for fattening, which benefits the owner.

phrases.english: His Canaanite slaves and maidservants:
are meant for work,
an animal is meant for fattening.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Slaves are kept for work, but animals are kept to be fattened, so feeding an animal benefits the owner.

steps.title: New משנה: visiting and healing the מודר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: when someone forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend comes to visit him, he stands and does not sit. The friend may heal him with רפואת נפש but not רפואת ממון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend, and he goes in to visit him, he stands but does not sit. And the friend may heal him with a healing of the body, but not a healing of money.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two rules: how the מודר may act while visiting, and what kind of healing his friend may give him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule limits the visit: standing is fine, sitting is not. The second rule splits healing into two types, רפואת נפש (allowed) and רפואת ממון (not allowed); the גמרא will explain these terms.

keyTerms.meaning: To visit him (usually a sick person)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say who is sick or what these two kinds of healing are. The גמרא on the next amud works these out, so don't guess yet.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who is forbidden by vow to benefit from his friend
and he goes in to visit him:
he stands but does not sit.
And he heals him with a healing of the body,
but not a healing of money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וְנִכְנַס לְבַקְּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the previous one ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a visit, the מודר stands but does not sit; his friend may give רפואת נפש but not רפואת ממון.
